subject: handoff from modmill-4r0.1 (high confidence)
body:
Inherited from modmill-4r0.1, closed by w1-samples.
Confidence: high — verified: tested, reproduced, or read from the source

1) Sample header is 30 bytes, starting at file offset 20+i*30 for sample i (0-indexed): name(22B)@0-21, length(2B)@22-23, finetune(1B)@24, volume(1B)@25, loop_start(2B)@26-27, loop_len(2B)@28-29 (all big-endian). 2) length/loop_start/loop_len are stored in WORDS not bytes — multiply by 2 before indexing PCM data; this is the most common parsing bug. 3) loop_len_words <= 1 means 'no loop' (one-shot) by PT convention — minimal.mod sample0 encodes this as loop_start=0,loop_len=1 (offsets 46-49), NOT a real 2-byte loop; must special-case before computing byte offsets. 4) finetune only uses the low nibble, signed: nibble 0-7 -> 0..+7, nibble 8-15 -> -8..-1 (two's complement); volume is linear 0-64 (0x40 max). 5) Nothing in the format prevents loop_start_bytes+loop_len_bytes > length_bytes; real PT does not validate and will read past the sample into adjacent pool data — parsers should clamp or drop the loop rather than reproduce that undefined read. Concrete example: loop.mod sample0 = length 32 words(64B), loop_start 8 words(16B), loop_len 16 words(32B) -> valid sustain loop [16,48) within a 64B sample. Full writeup with byte dumps in docs/format-notes/samples.md.

subject: handoff from modmill-4r0.2 (high confidence)
body:
Inherited from modmill-4r0.2, closed by w1-effects.
Confidence: high — verified: tested, reproduced, or read from the source

1) Effects apply starting tick 1, not tick 0: tick 0 is the note-trigger/rest tick (arpeggio's tick%3==0 index conveniently reads as base note too); C/D/B/F are row-level, decided once at tick 0, not per-tick. 2) F effect boundary at 0x20: param<0x20 sets speed (ticks/row), param>=0x20 sets tempo (BPM) directly as a plain integer -- confirmed in speed.mod (F03 speed=3, F78=120 BPM). F00 (speed=0) is an edge case that freezes row advance in real PT; needs an explicit no-op-or-halt policy to avoid an infinite loop. 3) D's param is packed BCD (two decimal digits: (param>>4)*10+(param&0xF)), NOT plain hex/binary like B and F -- jump.mod's pattern0 row0 has D10, which is row 10 decimal, not row 16 as the fixture generator's own comment claims; modmill-4r0.6 must not copy that comment's number into a test expectation. 4) B's param is a plain 0-based order-table index (confirmed jump.mod B02 -> order slot 2 -> pattern2, per the order table at offset 950). 5) When D and B land on the same row, B wins the destination pattern (order-table slot) and D wins the destination row within it; if only D appears the pattern defaults to order+1, if only B appears the row defaults to 0.
